items.title: Woman wanted after 71 vehicles targeted in Mississauga break-in spree
items.summary: Police are searching for a woman wanted in connection with a series of vehicle break-ins across Mississauga. Police Regional Police say the incidents happened during the early morning hours of Sept. 3 and Sept. 6 in neighbourhoods throughout the city. Investigators allege vehicles were entered by smashing windows or through unlocked doors and valuables were stolen. Police say 71 vehicles were involved in the investigation. No vehicles were stolen and all were unoccupied at the time. Andrea Cederberg, 33, of no fixed address, is wanted on 23 counts of attempting to commit an indictable offence, nine counts each of mischief over $5,000 and theft under $5,000, and one count of theft over $5,000. Police say the investigation is connected to the recent arrest of Cory Lowden, 34, of no fixed address. Investigators have also identified possible connections to similar vehicle-related crimes under investigation in Halton Region, Toronto, York Region and Waterloo Region. Police say they are working with other police services across the Greater Toronto Area to determine the full scope of the alleged activity.

items.title: 2nd suspect wanted in 71 vehicle break-ins in Mississauga
items.summary: Police are searching for a second suspect after 71 vehicle break-ins in Mississauga earlier this month. Police said on Saturday that the “large-scale break-in spree” occurred in the early morning hours of Sept. 3 and 6 throughout a number of neighbourhoods. “Investigators allege that vehicles were unlawfully entered, either by smashing windows or taking advantage of unlocked doors, and valuables were stolen,” police said. They noted that no vehicles were stolen and all were unoccupied during the incidents. In a news release on Saturday, police said 33-year-old Andrea Cederberg of no fixed address is wanted for 23 counts of attempt to commit an indictable offence, nine counts of mischief over $5,000, nine counts of theft under $5,000 and one count of theft over $5,000. The incidents involving Cederberg, police said, are connected to the arrest of 34-year-old Cory Lowden earlier this week. Lowden is facing more than 78 charges in connection with the incidents. Police said they have identified potential connections to similar incidents in Toronto, Halton, York and Waterloo regions.

items.title: Nearly 9,000 students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon suspended over vaccine records
items.summary: Peel Public Health warned parents last year that students could be suspended from school over missing vaccination records. It wasn’t an empty threat. A total of 8,875 students were suspended in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon during Peel’s 2025-26 immunization enforcement cycle, according to new figures provided by the region as thousands of students once again face scrutiny over their vaccination records. The number is significant because Peel Public Health is now warning that approximately 27,500 students will have their immunization records reviewed during the 2026-27 school year. The region says students with incomplete records could again face suspension if their information isn’t brought up to date or a valid exemption isn’t provided. The new figure comes months after Peel Public Health warned that 15,861 students were potentially facing suspension during the previous school year. At the time, the warning applied to students whose immunization records did not meet provincial requirements. Peel has now confirmed that 8,875 students were ultimately suspended during the full 2025-26 enforcement cycle. Peel says the 15,861 figure reported in March was a snapshot and changed from week to week as families submitted vaccination information. But the new number does establish something parents should take seriously: Peel does enforce the suspension provision.

items.title: Kelso’s chairlift rides offer sweeping views of peak fall colours
items.summary: Kelso Conservation Area’s chairlift opens Oct. 3. Kelso Conservation Area’s chairlifts offer sweeping fall views. Located less than an hour from Toronto, Kelso Conservation Area offers an elevated way to take in southern Ontario’s vibrant autumn foliage. ), the three-square-kilometre park features rolling terrain framed by Kelso Lake. Returning weekends and Thanksgiving Monday, from Oct. 3 to Nov. 1 (weather permitting), Kelso’s annual chairlift rides offer sweeping views of peak fall colours. Visitors can take a chairlift ride up the hills and back down, enjoying panoramic views of vivid red, orange, and yellow foliage set against the escarpment wall. At the top, hikers can explore the three-kilometre fall loop trail and visit the park’s main lookout point for additional photo opportunities. Updated trail maps featuring suggested hiking routes are coming soon to the official Conservation Halton website. Chairlift tickets are valid for two trips (in any combination of up or down) and must be added to your online park reservation. m. m.

items.title: Extra charge could soon be added to some parking fines in Mississauga
items.summary: Some vehicle owners who get parking tickets in Mississauga might soon be hit with an additional charge to cover costs associated with the city’s new way of delivering penalty notices. The mailing of tickets to registered owners of illegally parked cars is among several changes to City of Mississauga parking enforcement rules that will take effect Oct. 1. Parking tickets will still be left on vehicle windshields, but in cases where doing so could be dangerous or otherwise difficult for bylaw enforcement officers, the option will now be there to record the licence plate and the municipality will then send an infraction notice to the vehicle owner by mail. To cover costs associated with sending tickets by mail, senior city staff are proposing a $10 mail-out fee to be paid by those who receive such parking infraction notices. The proposal, included in a report from community services commissioner Raj Sheth, will be discussed by city councillors next Wednesday at general committee. “Serving a penalty notice by mail requires additional administrative steps to prepare, quality-check, process, print and mail the notice,” Sheth noted in his report. “Staff, therefore, recommend introducing a mail-out fee of $10 to recover the associated costs. ” Revenue from the fee “is expected to offset the costs incurred by the city in administering the mail-out process,” he added. The report concluded that parking tickets “will continue to be affixed directly to vehicles wherever it is safe and reasonably practicable to do so.

items.title: More than 200 years later, a Mississauga family’s War of 1812 story comes alive
items.summary: More than 200 years ago, a family settled on hundreds of acres of land in what is now part of Mississauga and soon found itself caught up in a war that would send four sons into battle, leave two of them prisoners of war and claim the life of another. This weekend, that story will come back to life at the very heart of the community where the family once lived. Engagement at Bradley, the annual War of 1812 living-history event at Mississauga’s Bradley Museum, returns Saturday and Sunday, bringing soldiers, military camps and battlefield demonstrations to the historic site. The War of 1812 was fought between the United States and Britain, but much of the conflict unfolded on what is now Canadian soil. S. expansionist ambitions, the war brought fighting to communities across Upper Canada and drew local settlers into military service. For many families in what is now Mississauga, it meant leaving farms and homes behind to help defend the colony. For the organizers, the event is about more than recreating a battle. It is a way of telling the stories of the people who actually lived through the conflict in what was then known as Toronto Township. Cornelius and Rebecca Thompson arrived from New Brunswick after Cornelius received a 480-acre land grant in Toronto Township in 1808. The family settled on the property the following year, building a log cabin before constructing a larger home they called Harwood. Their land was in the area that would eventually become Clarkson, just west of the property belonging to the Bradley family, whose historic home is now part of Bradley Museum. When the War of 1812 began, four of the Thompson sons — William, Augustus, Frederick and Cornelius Oliver — joined the 2nd Regiment of York Militia.

items.title: Winter prep starts earlier than ever at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Temperatures are still warm enough to walk around in Mississauga without a jacket, but preparations for winter have already begun at one particular place on the city’s eastern edge. m. on Sept. 1 — its earliest-ever start, according to the airport. “… a B737-800 MAX became the first aircraft (this season) to enter the (de-icing facility) for a frost spray — eight days earlier than last year and nearly three weeks earlier than the 2024-25 season,” Pearson officials said, adding the early aircraft de-icing comes on the heels of a record-breaking season for the large facility last winter. “As Canada’s largest and busiest airport, Pearson plays a critical role in keeping people, businesses and goods connected across Canada and around the world, including through challenging winter conditions,” officials continued in an online post. Last winter, 22,597 aircraft used the de-icing facility at Pearson, according to the airport. ” Airport officials said earlier that as of winter 2025, 53 pieces of specialized equipment — 46 de-icing trucks, four Glycol (antifreeze) recovery vehicles, three underwing de-icers — comprised Pearson’s de-icing facility. Toronto Pearson Airport’s fleet of winter maintenance equipment also includes dozens of snowplows in addition to dozens more snowblowers, front-end loaders, snow tractors, sweepers and other pieces of equipment.

items.title: Enjoy an evening of art, apples and agriculture
items.summary: Join us on October 1 for Homegrown Mississauga: Apples, Art & Seed Saving, a free community event that celebrates local food, gardening and public art. Growing food, whether in a backyard, on a balcony, or in a community garden, brings people together and helps make our city greener and more resilient to the impacts of climate change. The City of Mississauga supports urban agriculture by helping residents access fresh local food and creating more opportunities to learn and share with one another. To celebrate urban agriculture and the end of the growing season, we invite residents to join us at the Small Arms Inspection Building for an evening of learning, connection and local food. The event includes: A free, in-person event that highlights urban agriculture and gardening activities in Mississauga. m. Small Arms Inspection Building, 1352 Lakeshore Rd. E, Mississauga. Free. Online registration is recommended as space is limited. Everyone is welcome. Children under 12 must attend with an adult. Want to learn more about growing food at home? The City’s growing guides offer tips for planting, caring for, and harvesting fruits and vegetables.

items.title: Via Rail’s plan to cut Guildwood, Malton service and reduce eastern Ontario trains sparks outcry
items.summary: The Crown corporation says the changes will roll out Oct. 25 and affect routes along the Ottawa-Toronto corridor. Via Rail will be rolling out its new schedule on Oct. 25. Via Rail says it will no longer serve Toronto-area stations Guildwood and Malton later this fall as it rolls out multiple adjustments and reduced train service along select routes. The upcoming changes, announced Wednesday and set to begin Oct. 25, will also affect service along the Ottawa-Toronto corridor, including stops in Kingston and Cobourg, sparking sharp criticism from municipal leaders. m. train from the nation’s capital to Toronto. “The revised schedule will better align service with passenger demand, strengthen network resilience and support more reliable and predictable service,” Via Rail wrote in a news release. Via Rail said the removal of stops at Guildwood in Scarborough and the Malton in Mississauga will “improve overall travel times,” citing the stations’ proximity to Union Station in downtown Toronto and the availability of GO Transit and other services. Scarborough councillor and Toronto deputy mayor Paul Ainslie slammed Via’s decision, calling on the transit agency to reverse it.

items.title: Beat the lines on Election Day. Vote in the Advance Polls
items.summary: Voters can get an early start on Mississauga’s 2026 Municipal Election with advance voting taking place from October 6 to 11. The City of Mississauga encourages eligible voters to take advantage of advance voting before Election Day, Monday, October 26. Advance voting gives voters more days and more locations to cast their ballot before Election Day. It is the same voting process, offered earlier, so you can choose a time that works best for you. Advance voting helps make voting easier, reduces lineups and gives voters more flexibility. If you have work, school, caregiving responsibilities, travel plans or other commitments on October 26, advance voting can help you make a plan and have your say. Vote in advance from Tuesday, October 6 to Sunday, October 11. ) on October 6 and 7. From October 8 to 11, locations will be open across the city, and you can vote at any advance voting location. On Election Day, eligible voters may vote at a voting location in the ward in which they live or have property. You will elect the Mayor, Ward/Regional Councillor and School Board Trustees. Bring your Voter notification card (if you receive one) and one piece of acceptable identification. Before you vote, take a few minutes to make sure you are eligible, your voter information is correct and you know where you can cast your ballot. This helps make the voting process faster and helps election staff give you the right ballot.

items.title: Don’t let water quality go down the drain this pool season
items.summary: Getting ready to close your outdoor pool? A few simple steps can help keep chemicals out of the stormwater system and protect Lake Ontario, the source of Mississauga's drinking water. Many Mississauga homes have backyard pools that need to be drained and winterized before colder weather arrives. If you’re closing your outdoor pool for the winter, it’s important to do it safely and responsibly. Prevent pool chemicals from entering waterways and harming wildlife by disposing of them the right way. This helps protect your health and our environment. Remove leaves, grass and other debris from the water. This helps keep the water cleaner over the winter. If you have an automatic pool cleaner, remove it, drain it, let it dry and store it until next season. Test the pool water for chlorine and pH levels. 0, which is neutral. After treatment, do not add any more chemicals or algae-control products for at least seven days. Before draining any water, make sure the chlorine level is zero. Pool and spa owners must follow the City of Mississauga’s by-law when draining water.
